evidenceAudit.scope: Adults referred for cataract surgery: referral decision, information, biometry and peri-operative antibiotic prophylaxis. Verified against NICE NG77 and NG45 (minor/intermediate tests) and Saudi MOH Protocol-015 (ophthalmic prophylaxis).
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 12 Oct 2026.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: NICE NG77 intracameral antibiotic recommendations not reviewed this run
SFDA registration not checked per drug
Local antibiogram may add gentamicin (MOH p. 1)

pathophysiology.summary: A cataract is opacification of the lens, scattering light and reducing visual quality. Surgery replaces the lens with an intraocular lens chosen by biometry.
keyMechanisms: Lens protein changes with age, diabetes, steroids or trauma cause opacity and glare.
Axial length and corneal curvature determine intraocular lens power — biometry (NICE NG77).
Endophthalmitis is rare but serious — topical/intracameral antibiotic prophylaxis (MOH).

symptoms: Blurred or dim vision, glare, difficulty reading or driving.
physicalSigns: Reduced visual acuity; lens opacity on slit lamp; reduced red reflex.
redFlags: Sudden visual loss or eye pain — not cataract: urgent ophthalmology
Post-operative pain, redness or vision drop — endophthalmitis

clinicalManagement.title: Referral
actions: Base referral on impact on vision and quality of life, one or both eyes, risks and benefits, and the person's wish for surgery — not on visual acuity alone (NICE NG77).

clinicalManagement.title: Preparation
actions: Explain refractive outcomes, anaesthesia, individual complication risks (e.g. retinal detachment in high myopia), anticoagulants and eye drops (NICE NG77).
Most cataract surgery needs no routine blood tests in ASA 1–2 (NICE NG45 minor surgery table).

clinicalManagement.title: Pre-operative assessment
actions: Grade surgery (minor, intermediate, major/complex) and ASA status; order only the tests NICE NG45 lists for that combination.
Do not routinely order chest X-ray, urine dipstick, sickle tests or HbA1c in people without diabetes (NICE NG45).
Discuss stopping smoking and reducing alcohol; manage iron-deficiency anaemia (NICE NG180).
Make an individual anticoagulant plan if the person takes anticoagulants (NICE NG45).

clinicalManagement.title: VTE prophylaxis
actions: Assess individual VTE risk on admission per NICE NG89 — no cataract-specific VTE recommendation was reviewed.

clinicalManagement.title: Surgical antibiotic prophylaxis (MOH Protocol-015)
actions: Ophthalmic: topical moxifloxacin 1 drop every 5–15 min for 5 doses; optional intracameral cefazolin 1–2.5 mg or subconjunctival cefazolin 100 mg (MOH p. 3).
Re-dose cefazolin every 4 h (or clindamycin every 6 h) if surgery lasts more than 4 h or blood loss exceeds 1,500 mL (MOH p. 1).
Stop prophylaxis within 24 h of the end of surgery, even with drains or catheters (MOH p. 4).

learningObjectives: Assess adults for cataract surgery and prepare them safely.

pitfalls: Missing other eye disease limiting outcome.

patientEducation: Post-op eye drops, warning signs (pain, redness, vision loss), driving restrictions (NICE NG77).
lifestyleAndDiet: Stop smoking and reduce alcohol before surgery (NICE NG180).
Stay active; prehabilitation exercises where advised.
dischargeCriteria: Pain controlled with oral analgesia; eating, drinking and mobilising.
Wound satisfactory; VTE prophylaxis plan and follow-up arranged.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Post-operative review per surgical team; return immediately with fever, wound redness, calf swelling, breathlessness or chest pain.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Based on vision and quality of life, not acuity threshold (NICE NG77)
Optical first; ultrasound if not possible
